seed: In the next 6-12 months, the United States and China engage in a series of escalating trade tariffs, leading to significant disruptions in global supply chains and increased inflation rates worldwide.

nodes.text: In the next 6-12 months, the United States and China engage in a series of escalating trade tariffs, leading to significant disruptions in global supply chains and increased inflation rates worldwide.
Tariff impact – US steel and aluminum exports to China decrease by $5–8B, affecting global prices within 6 months.

profit.idea: Diversify supply chains to mitigate tariff impacts.
profit.explanation: By sourcing materials from alternative countries, businesses can reduce dependency on affected markets and stabilize costs.

nodes.text: Commodity price surge – Oil prices rise by $10–15 per barrel as Middle Eastern producers limit supply in response to trade tensions (6–9 months).

profit.idea: Diversify supply sources to mitigate risks.
profit.explanation: By sourcing oil from a wider range of suppliers, businesses can reduce dependency on Middle Eastern producers and stabilize costs.

nodes.text: Agricultural shifts – US wheat and rice exports to Asia drop by $3–5B, leading to increased domestic prices within 12 months.

profit.idea: Diversify export markets for wheat and rice.
profit.explanation: Expanding into emerging markets can mitigate losses from reduced exports to Asia and stabilize revenue.

nodes.text: Consumer electronics slowdown – Samsung and LG face a 10–15% decline in sales revenue due to rising tariffs on components (9–12 months).

profit.idea: Diversify supply chain sources to mitigate tariff impacts.
profit.explanation: By sourcing components from various suppliers, companies can reduce dependency on affected regions and stabilize costs.
